angle: Coffee feels global, but the map of where it grows is very concentrated: in the US Department of Agriculture's 2026/27 forecast, Brazil and Vietnam alone grow 55% of the world's coffee and five countries three-quarters, while the biggest drinkers, Europe and the United States, import nearly all of theirs.
paragraphs: More than half of the world's coffee comes from just two countries.
Number one is Brazil. This season, the US Department of Agriculture expects a record {seventy-one point nine million bags|71.9 million bags}. Almost two bags in every five on Earth.
Number two isn't Colombia. It's Vietnam: {thirty-two point five million bags|32.5 million}, almost all of it robusta.
Together, Brazil and Vietnam grow {fifty-five percent|55%} of the world's coffee.
Colombia, Ethiopia and Indonesia come next. Between them, about one bag in five.
Then the beans cross the oceans. The European Union imports {fifty million bags|50 million} a year. The United States, almost {twenty-seven million|27 million}: nearly everything it drinks.
Two countries grow more than half of the world's coffee. More on the channel.
